421	def version_option(
422	    version: str | None = None,
423	    *param_decls: str,
424	    package_name: str | None = None,
425	    prog_name: str | None = None,
426	    message: str | None = None,
427	    **kwargs: t.Any,
428	) -> t.Callable[[FC], FC]:
429	    """Add a ``--version`` option which immediately prints the version
430	    number and exits the program.
431	
432	    If ``version`` is not provided, Click will try to detect it using
433	    :func:`importlib.metadata.version` to get the version for the
434	    ``package_name``.
435	
436	    If ``package_name`` is not provided, Click will try to detect it by
437	    inspecting the stack frames. If the detected (or given) name does
438	    not match an installed distribution, Click resolves it as an import
439	    (top-level module) name via
440	    :func:`importlib.metadata.packages_distributions`, so e.g. ``PIL``
441	    resolves to the ``Pillow`` distribution.
442	
443	    .. note::
444	        The parameters and message variables accepted by this option are
445	        frozen: no new slots will be added, to keep the common case simple
446	        and predictable. If you need values it does not expose, such as a
447	        file path, the Python version, or git metadata, use
448	        :func:`custom_version_option` to render the output yourself.
449	
450	        Rationale: `discussion #3527
451	        <https://github.com/pallets/click/discussions/3527>`_.
452	
453	    :param version: The version number to show. If not provided, Click
454	        will try to detect it.
455	    :param param_decls: One or more option names. Defaults to the single
456	        value ``"--version"``.
457	    :param package_name: The package name to detect the version from. If
458	        not provided, Click will try to detect it.
459	    :param prog_name: The name of the CLI to show in the message. If not
460	        provided, it will be detected from the command.
461	    :param message: The message to show. The values ``%(prog)s``,
462	        ``%(package)s``, and ``%(version)s`` are available. Defaults to
463	        ``"%(prog)s, version %(version)s"``.
464	    :param kwargs: Extra arguments are passed to :func:`option`.
465	    :raise RuntimeError: ``version`` could not be detected.
466	
467	    .. versionchanged:: 8.0
468	        Add the ``package_name`` parameter, and the ``%(package)s``
469	        value for messages.
470	
471	    .. versionchanged:: 8.0
472	        Use :mod:`importlib.metadata` instead of ``pkg_resources``. The
473	        version is detected based on the package name, not the entry
474	        point name. The Python package name must match the installed
475	        package name, or be passed with ``package_name=``.
476	
477	    .. versionchanged:: 8.4.2
478	        When ``package_name`` does not match an installed distribution,
479	        Click now resolves it as an import (top-level module).
480	    """
481	    if message is None:
482	        message = _("%(prog)s, version %(version)s")
483	
484	    if version is None and package_name is None:
485	        frame = inspect.currentframe()
486	        f_back = frame.f_back if frame is not None else None
487	        f_globals = f_back.f_globals if f_back is not None else None
488	        # break reference cycle
489	        # https://docs.python.org/3/library/inspect.html#the-interpreter-stack
490	        del frame
491	
492	        if f_globals is not None:
493	            package_name = f_globals.get("__name__")
494	
495	            if package_name == "__main__":
496	                package_name = f_globals.get("__package__")
497	
498	            if package_name:
499	                package_name = package_name.partition(".")[0]
500	
501	    def callback(ctx: Context, param: Parameter, value: bool) -> None:
502	        if not value or ctx.resilient_parsing:
503	            return
504	
505	        nonlocal prog_name
506	        nonlocal version
507	        nonlocal package_name
508	
509	        if prog_name is None:
510	            prog_name = ctx.find_root().info_name
511	
512	        if version is None and package_name is not None:
513	            import importlib.metadata
514	
515	            try:
516	                version = importlib.metadata.version(package_name)
517	            except importlib.metadata.PackageNotFoundError:
518	                # The given name didn't match an installed distribution.
519	                # Try resolving it as an import (top-level module) name,
520	                # e.g. ``PIL`` is provided by the ``Pillow`` distribution.
521	                distributions = importlib.metadata.packages_distributions().get(
522	                    package_name, []
523	                )
524	                if len(distributions) == 1:
525	                    package_name = distributions[0]
526	                    version = importlib.metadata.version(package_name)
527	                elif len(distributions) > 1:
528	                    raise RuntimeError(
529	                        f"{package_name!r} maps to multiple installed"
530	                        f" distributions ({', '.join(distributions)})."
531	                        " Pass 'package_name' to disambiguate."
532	                    ) from None
533	                else:
534	                    raise RuntimeError(
535	                        f"{package_name!r} is not installed. Try passing"
536	                        " 'package_name' instead."
537	                    ) from None
538	
539	        if version is None:
540	            raise RuntimeError(
541	                f"Could not determine the version for {package_name!r} automatically."
542	            )
543	
544	        echo(
545	            message % {"prog": prog_name, "package": package_name, "version": version},
546	            color=ctx.color,
547	        )
548	        ctx.exit()
549	
550	    if not param_decls:
551	        param_decls = ("--version",)
552	
553	    kwargs.setdefault("is_flag", True)
554	    kwargs.setdefault("expose_value", False)
555	    kwargs.setdefault("is_eager", True)
556	    kwargs.setdefault("help", _("Show the version and exit."))
557	    kwargs["callback"] = callback
558	    return option(*param_decls, **kwargs)
559

561	def custom_version_option(
562	    callback: t.Callable[[Context], str],
563	    *param_decls: str,
564	    **kwargs: t.Any,
565	) -> t.Callable[[FC], FC]:
566	    """Add a ``--version`` option whose output is produced by ``callback``.
567	
568	    This is the customizable companion to :func:`version_option`. Where
569	    :func:`version_option` is intentionally limited to a fixed message and
570	    a small set of values, this option calls ``callback`` to build the
571	    whole string to print. Use it when you need values that
572	    :func:`version_option` does not expose, such as a file path, the
573	    Python version, or git metadata.
574	
575	    :param callback: Called with the current :class:`Context` when the
576	        option is invoked. Its return value is printed, then the program
577	        exits.
578	    :param param_decls: One or more option names. Defaults to the single
579	        value ``--version``.
580	    :param kwargs: Extra arguments are passed to :func:`option`.
581	
582	    .. versionadded:: 8.5.0
583	    """
584	
585	    def show_version(ctx: Context, param: Parameter, value: bool) -> None:
586	        if not value or ctx.resilient_parsing:
587	            return
588	
589	        echo(callback(ctx), color=ctx.color)
590	        ctx.exit()
591	
592	    if not param_decls:
593	        param_decls = ("--version",)
594	
595	    kwargs.setdefault("is_flag", True)
596	    kwargs.setdefault("expose_value", False)
597	    kwargs.setdefault("is_eager", True)
598	    kwargs.setdefault("help", _("Show the version and exit."))
599	    kwargs["callback"] = show_version
600	    return option(*param_decls, **kwargs)

604	    """Pre-configured ``--help`` option which immediately prints the help page
605	    and exits the program.

608	        value ``"--help"``.
609	    :param kwargs: Extra arguments are passed to :func:`option`.

613	        """Callback that print the help page on ``<stdout>`` and exits."""

616	            ctx.exit()

618	    if not param_decls:
619	        param_decls = ("--help",)

624	    kwargs.setdefault("help", _("Show this message and exit."))
625	    kwargs.setdefault("callback", show_help)

359	        for plain strings) to enable type-checked consumers.

363	        iterable. Before you were not recommended to pass anything but a list or
364	        tuple.

368	    """

372	    choices: tuple[_ValueT_co, ...]

375	    def __init__(
376	        self, choices: cabc.Iterable[_ValueT_co], case_sensitive: bool = True
377	    ) -> None:
378	        self.choices = tuple(choices)

388	    def _normalized_mapping(
389	        self, ctx: Context | None = None
390	    ) -> cabc.Mapping[_ValueT_co, str]:
391	        """
392	        Returns mapping where keys are the original choices and the values are
393	        the normalized values that are accepted via the command line.
394	
395	        This is a simple wrapper around :meth:`normalize_choice`, use that
396	        instead which is supported.
397	        """
398	        return {
399	            choice: self.normalize_choice(
400	                choice=choice,
401	                ctx=ctx,
402	            )
403	            for choice in self.choices

406	    def normalize_choice(self, choice: object, ctx: Context | None) -> str:
407	        """
408	        Normalize a choice value, used to map a passed string to a choice.
409	        Each choice must have a unique normalized value.
410	
411	        By default uses :meth:`Context.token_normalize_func` and if not case
412	        sensitive, convert it to a casefolded value.
413	
414	        .. versionadded:: 8.2.0
415	        """
416	        normed_value = choice.name if isinstance(choice, enum.Enum) else str(choice)
417	
418	        if ctx is not None and ctx.token_normalize_func is not None:
419	            normed_value = ctx.token_normalize_func(normed_value)
420	
421	        if not self.case_sensitive:
422	            normed_value = normed_value.casefold()
423	
424	        return normed_value

426	    def get_metavar(self, param: Parameter, ctx: Context) -> str | None:
427	        if param.param_type_name == "option" and not param.show_choices:  # type: ignore[attr-defined]

429	                convert_type(type(choice)).name.upper() for choice in self.choices
430	            ]
431	            choices_str = "|".join([*dict.fromkeys(choice_metavars)])
432	        else:
433	            choices_str = "|".join(
434	                [str(i) for i in self._normalized_mapping(ctx=ctx).values()]
435	            )

438	        if param.required and param.param_type_name == "argument":

452	        )

454	    def convert(
455	        self, value: t.Any, param: Parameter | None, ctx: Context | None
456	    ) -> _ValueT_co:

459	        matching normalized value in the list of choices. Then return the
460	        matched "original" choice.

463	        normalized_mapping = self._normalized_mapping(ctx=ctx)

469	                if normalized == normed_value

471	        except StopIteration:

473	                self.get_invalid_choice_message(value=value, ctx=ctx),

486	        return ngettext(

495	    def shell_complete(
496	        self, ctx: Context, param: Parameter, incomplete: str
497	    ) -> list[CompletionItem]:
498	        """Complete choices that start with the incomplete value.
499	
500	        :param ctx: Invocation context for this command.
501	        :param param: The parameter that is requesting completion.
502	        :param incomplete: Value being completed. May be empty.
503	
504	        .. versionadded:: 8.0
505	        """
506	        from click.shell_completion import CompletionItem
507	
508	        str_choices = [self.normalize_choice(choice, ctx) for choice in self.choices]
509	        if self.case_sensitive:

511	        else:
512	            incomplete = incomplete.lower()
513	            matched = (c for c in str_choices if c.lower().startswith(incomplete))

645	        max: _FloatValueT_co | None = None,
646	        min_open: bool = False,

668	    ) -> _FloatValueT_co:
669	        import operator
670	
671	        rv = super().convert(value, param, ctx)
672	        min = self.min
673	        max = self.max
674	        lt_min: bool = min is not None and (
675	            operator.le if self.min_open else operator.lt

679	        )(rv, max)

681	        if self.clamp:

683	                return self._clamp(min, 1, self.min_open)
684	
685	            if max is not None and gt_max:
686	                return self._clamp(max, -1, self.max_open)

688	        if lt_min or gt_max:
689	            self.fail(
690	                _("{value} is not in the range {range}.").format(

692	                ),

718	        """Describe the range for use in help text."""

722	
723	        if self.max is None:

=== 0f71fe7
Fix dual-option arbitration to respect explicit defaults

Closes #3403

=== 7d05a59
Fix get_parameter_source() during type conversion and eager callbacks

Record parameter source on the context immediately after consume_value(),
before process_value() runs. In 8.4.0, set_parameter_source() was deferred
until after type conversion and flag-group arbitration (0f71fe7, #3403), so
get_parameter_source() returned None inside ParamType.convert() and eager
callbacks (#3458).

When several options share one parameter name, the losing option still sets a
provisional source before process_value(); restore the previous source if
arbitration rejects it so the winner's origin is not replaced unintentionally.

"""Reproduce the env var hint formatting issues in help output and error messages.

Run: .venv/bin/python /tmp/click-probe/repro_envvar_hint.py
"""

import click
from click.testing import CliRunner

CASES = {
    "list of two": ["WEATHER_UNITS", "UNITS"],
    "empty string": "",
    "empty list": [],
    "single string (control)": "WEATHER_UNITS",
}


def make_cli(envvar):
    @click.command()
    @click.option(
        "--units",
        type=click.Choice(["metric", "imperial"]),
        envvar=envvar,
        show_envvar=True,
        help="Units to use.",
    )
    def cli(units):
        click.echo(f"units={units}")

    return cli


runner = CliRunner()

for label, envvar in CASES.items():
    cli = make_cli(envvar)
    print(f"=== envvar={envvar!r}  ({label})")

    help_result = runner.invoke(cli, ["--help"])
    help_line = next(
        line for line in help_result.output.splitlines() if "--units" in line
    )
    print(f"  help : {help_line.strip()}")

    err_result = runner.invoke(cli, ["--units", "kelvin"])
    err_line = next(
        line for line in err_result.output.splitlines() if line.startswith("Error:")
    )
    print(f"  error: {err_line}  (exit {err_result.exit_code})")
    print()

5	- Fix `copy.deepcopy()` and `pickle` on a `Parameter`, `Option` or `Command`. {pr}`3805`
6	- A `KeyboardInterrupt` arriving while `Command.main()` reports an abort or an error,
7	  or while it exits, no longer escapes as an unhandled traceback. The command still
8	  exits with the intended code; only the message may be lost. {issue}`3802`
9	- Add {meth}`Option.get_help_spec`, which returns the option's left help
10	  column even when the option is hidden. {meth}`Option.get_help_record` still
11	  returns `None` for hidden options, so help screens are unchanged. {pr}`3821`
12	- The `Positional arguments` help section lists every argument of the command,
13	  not only the documented ones. An argument with no `help` gets an empty
14	  description, the same way an option with no `help` does. {pr}`3860`
15	- {meth}`Argument.get_help_record` always returns a tuple. It used to return
16	  `None` for an argument with no `help`. {pr}`3860`
17	- Document which types are inferred from `default`, and what an unrecognized
18	  `type` callable does to a command-line value. {issue}`3036` {pr}`3808`
19	- `path_type` narrows the converted value's type for `convert` and `prompt`.
20	  {issue}`3822` {pr}`3858`
21	- {class}`Parameter` accepts a new `help` argument and {class}`Option` and {class}`Argument`
22	  inherits it. {meth}`Parameter.to_info_dict` now reports `help` for every kind of parameter.
23	  {pr}`3861`
24	- A command's short help no longer stops at an abbreviation such as `vs.` or `e.g.`
25	  inside the first sentence. A period ends the sentence only when it closes the text

1	## Version 8.5.1
2	
3	Unreleased
4	
5	- Fix `copy.deepcopy()` and `pickle` on a `Parameter`, `Option` or `Command`. {pr}`3805`
6	- A `KeyboardInterrupt` arriving while `Command.main()` reports an abort or an error,
7	  or while it exits, no longer escapes as an unhandled traceback. The command still
8	  exits with the intended code; only the message may be lost. {issue}`3802`
9	- Add {meth}`Option.get_help_spec`, which returns the option's left help
10	  column even when the option is hidden. {meth}`Option.get_help_record` still
11	  returns `None` for hidden options, so help screens are unchanged. {pr}`3821`
12	- The `Positional arguments` help section lists every argument of the command,
13	  not only the documented ones. An argument with no `help` gets an empty
14	  description, the same way an option with no `help` does. {pr}`3860`
15	- {meth}`Argument.get_help_record` always returns a tuple. It used to return
16	  `None` for an argument with no `help`. {pr}`3860`
17	- Document which types are inferred from `default`, and what an unrecognized
18	  `type` callable does to a command-line value. {issue}`3036` {pr}`3808`
19	- `path_type` narrows the converted value's type for `convert` and `prompt`.
20	  {issue}`3822` {pr}`3858`
21	- {class}`Parameter` accepts a new `help` argument and {class}`Option` and {class}`Argument`
22	  inherits it. {meth}`Parameter.to_info_dict` now reports `help` for every kind of parameter.
23	  {pr}`3861`
24	- A command's short help no longer stops at an abbreviation such as `vs.` or `e.g.`
25	  inside the first sentence. A period ends the sentence only when it closes the text
26	  or the next word does not start in lowercase. {pr}`3865`
27	- With `show_envvar`, an option whose `envvar` is a list shows its names joined
28	  by commas in error messages, instead of the list's Python repr. An empty
29	  `envvar` (`""` or `[]`) no longer shows an empty `env var` in the help or in
30	  error messages.
31	
32	## Version 8.5.0
33	
34	Released 2026-08-24
35	
36	- Add built-in shell completion support for PowerShell (Windows PowerShell
37	  5.1+ and pwsh 7+) alongside the existing `bash`, `zsh`, and `fish`
38	  completers. Use `_FOO_BAR_COMPLETE=powershell_source foo-bar` to generate
39	  the completion script. {issue}`2672` {pr}`3637`
40	- Supported versions of Windows enable ANSI terminal styles by default.
41	  Colorama is no longer a dependency and is not used. {issue}`2986` {pr}`3505`
42	- {class}`Argument` accepts a `help` parameter, and help output includes
43	  a `Positional arguments` section when argument help is available. {issue}`2983` {pr}`3473`
44	- `confirm()` and `prompt()` strip ANSI color and style codes from the
45	  prompt when the output stream does not support them, matching `echo()`.
46	  This stripping was lost in `8.4.0` when {pr}`2969` began writing the
47	  prompt with `input()` directly. {issue}`3572` {pr}`3653`
48	- Fix test failures when using pytest >= 9.1. {pr}`3656`
49	- {class}`Path` with `allow_dash=True` no longer triggers a `BytesWarning`,
50	  an error under `python -bb`, when checking a value against the `-`
51	  convention. {issue}`2877` {pr}`3642`
52	- Add {func}`custom_version_option`, a `--version` option whose output is
53	  produced by a callback, covering cases {func}`version_option` intentionally
54	  does not. The feature set of {func}`version_option` is now frozen; see
55	  [discussion #3527](https://github.com/pallets/click/discussions/3527). {pr}`3581`
56	- `style()` and `secho()` no longer silently drop the 256-color index `0`
57	  (black) passed as `fg` or `bg`, and now validate color arguments. Invalid
58	  colors raise a `ValueError` instead of a `TypeError`. {pr}`3677`
59	- The automatic help option stores its value under the reserved name
60	  `_click_default_help` instead of `help`, so a parameter named `help` no
61	  longer breaks parsing. The new name is visible in
62	  {meth}`Command.to_info_dict` output. Parameters that overwrite each other's
63	  value trigger a warning: an argument sharing its name with another
64	  parameter, or any parameter claiming the reserved name. Options may still
65	  share a name to compete for the same value (feature switches).
66	  {issue}`2819` {pr}`3678`
67	- `unstyle` and the ANSI handling behind help-text wrapping now strip the full
68	  CSI escape-sequence grammar. {pr}`3681`
69	- Streamline `Option` flag handling: the flag-kind, type, lazy-default and
70	  validation steps in `Option.__init__` move into focused helpers, and
71	  `flag_value` and `default` keep their unset sentinel at construction
72	  (resolved lazily on read) so `is UNSET` reliably tells a user-supplied value
73	  from an auto-derived one. Runtime behavior is unchanged, but
74	  {meth}`Parameter.to_info_dict` now resolves `default=True` on a feature
75	  switch to its `flag_value`, matching what the function receives at call
76	  time. {pr}`3641`
77	- {func}`get_binary_stream` and {func}`get_text_stream` are deprecated and
78	  will be removed in Click 9.0. {issue}`3481` {pr}`3695`
79	- The following `click.utils` names were never intentionally public and are
80	  now private (`_`-prefixed). The old names remain available with a
81	  `DeprecationWarning` until Click 9.0: `LazyFile`, `KeepOpenFile`,
82	  `make_default_short_help`, `PacifyFlushWrapper`, and `safecall`.
83	  {issue}`3099` {pr}`3695`
84	- Deprecate {meth}`CliRunner.isolated_filesystem`. It relies on
85	  {func}`os.chdir`, which mutates process-global state and is not
86	  thread-safe. The helper predates Python 3 and modern pytest: use a
87	  temporary directory ({class}`tempfile.TemporaryDirectory` or pytest's
88	  `tmp_path` fixture) with absolute paths instead. For running tests in
89	  parallel, use process-based isolation (such as `pytest-xdist`) rather
90	  than threads, since {meth}`CliRunner.invoke` also redirects the
91	  process-global standard streams. {issue}`3501` {issue}`3700` {pr}`3704`
92	- `prompt()` is now generically typed and returns the type produced by
93	  `type`, `value_proc`, or a matching `default` instead of `Any`.
94	  {class}`ParamType` takes a second optional type parameter describing the
95	  input value it accepts (`ParamType[int, str]` for a type converting
96	  strings to integers), defaulting to `Any`. {pr}`3407`
97	- {meth}`Command.get_help_option_names` returns the help option names in the
98	  order they were declared. {pr}`3728`
99	- {func}`get_pager_file` yields a text stream on Windows again. The temporary
100	  file backend opened its file in binary mode, so writing a `str` to the pager
101	  raised `TypeError: a bytes-like object is required, not 'str'`, and the
102	  `color` argument was ignored on that path. Regression introduced in `8.4.0`
103	  by {pr}`1572`. {issue}`3731` {issue}`3732` {issue}`3740` {pr}`3739`
104	- {func}`progressbar` settles on its final position when `update_min_steps`
105	  does not divide the total. Steps below that threshold are applied when the
106	  bar finishes, so `show_pos` renders `20/20` rather than the last multiple
107	  it reached. {issue}`3571` {pr}`3769`
108	- An error raised while writing to the pager no longer gets replaced by
109	  `PermissionError: [WinError 32]` on Windows. The temporary file backend
110	  unlinked its file without closing it first, and Windows refuses to remove a
111	  file the process still holds open, so the cleanup failure masked the real
112	  exception. {issue}`3731` {pr}`3764`
113	- The temporary file the pager writes to on Windows is opened with the encoding

608	### Value sources
609	
610	Click resolves the value of every option from the following
611	sources, in order of decreasing precedence:
612	
613	1. **command line input** ({attr}`ParameterSource.COMMANDLINE`),
614	2. **environment variable** named in `envvar=` or derived from `auto_envvar_prefix`
615	   ({attr}`ParameterSource.ENVIRONMENT`),
616	3. **`default_map` entry** matching the parameter name on the active {class}`Context`
617	   ({attr}`ParameterSource.DEFAULT_MAP`),
618	4. **parameter default** ({attr}`ParameterSource.DEFAULT`).
619	
620	The first source that produces a value wins. Environment variables and
621	`default_map` entries set to `Sentinel.UNSET` are skipped, so they fall through
622	to the next source rather than supplying `UNSET` to the function.
623	
624	If after the four sources above no explicit value was found (or only a
625	`default_map`/`default` value was) and the option declares `prompt=`, Click
626	prompts the user for one. The resulting value is recorded as
627	{attr}`ParameterSource.PROMPT`, which ranks above every source listed above
628	for arbitration purposes (see [Slot arbitration](#slot-arbitration)).
629	
630	### Slot arbitration
631	
632	Several options can target the same `name` to form a feature switch group. When
633	they do, only one option's value reaches the function. Arbitration applies
634	these rules, in order:
635	
636	1. **By source.** Whichever option resolved its value from the most explicit
637	   source wins, regardless of decorator order. Any command-line input beats any
638	   default, an environment variable beats a `default_map` entry, and so on.
639	2. **Within the default tier, explicit beats auto-derived.** An option that
640	   received an explicit `default=` keyword wins over one whose default came
641	   from `default` interpretation.
642	3. **Otherwise, last declared wins.** When all options in the group resolved
643	   from the same source and tier (all auto-derived defaults, or all explicit
644	   defaults), the option declared last in the source code keeps the slot.
645

647

653	    @click.command()

657	
658	.. click:run::
659	
660	    invoke(greet, env={'USERNAME': 'john'})
661	```
662	
663	If a list is passed to `envvar`, the first environment variable found is picked.

672	
673	.. click:run::
674	
675	    invoke(greet, env={'ALT_USERNAME': 'Bill', 'USERNAME': 'john'})

677	```

## Version 8.5.1

Unreleased

- Fix `copy.deepcopy()` and `pickle` on a `Parameter`, `Option` or `Command`. {pr}`3805`
- A `KeyboardInterrupt` arriving while `Command.main()` reports an abort or an error,
  or while it exits, no longer escapes as an unhandled traceback. The command still
  exits with the intended code; only the message may be lost. {issue}`3802`
- Add {meth}`Option.get_help_spec`, which returns the option's left help
  column even when the option is hidden. {meth}`Option.get_help_record` still
  returns `None` for hidden options, so help screens are unchanged. {pr}`3821`
- The `Positional arguments` help section lists every argument of the command,
  not only the documented ones. An argument with no `help` gets an empty
  description, the same way an option with no `help` does. {pr}`3860`
- {meth}`Argument.get_help_record` always returns a tuple. It used to return
  `None` for an argument with no `help`. {pr}`3860`
- Document which types are inferred from `default`, and what an unrecognized
  `type` callable does to a command-line value. {issue}`3036` {pr}`3808`
- `path_type` narrows the converted value's type for `convert` and `prompt`.
  {issue}`3822` {pr}`3858`
- {class}`Parameter` accepts a new `help` argument and {class}`Option` and {class}`Argument`
  inherits it. {meth}`Parameter.to_info_dict` now reports `help` for every kind of parameter.
  {pr}`3861`
- A command's short help no longer stops at an abbreviation such as `vs.` or `e.g.`
  inside the first sentence. A period ends the sentence only when it closes the text
  or the next word does not start in lowercase. {pr}`3865`

## Version 8.5.0

Released 2026-08-24

32	## Version 8.5.0
33	
34	Released 2026-08-24
35	
36	- Add built-in shell completion support for PowerShell (Windows PowerShell
37	  5.1+ and pwsh 7+) alongside the existing `bash`, `zsh`, and `fish`
38	  completers. Use `_FOO_BAR_COMPLETE=powershell_source foo-bar` to generate
39	  the completion script. {issue}`2672` {pr}`3637`
40	- Supported versions of Windows enable ANSI terminal styles by default.
41	  Colorama is no longer a dependency and is not used. {issue}`2986` {pr}`3505`
42	- {class}`Argument` accepts a `help` parameter, and help output includes
43	  a `Positional arguments` section when argument help is available. {issue}`2983` {pr}`3473`
44	- `confirm()` and `prompt()` strip ANSI color and style codes from the
45	  prompt when the output stream does not support them, matching `echo()`.
46	  This stripping was lost in `8.4.0` when {pr}`2969` began writing the
47	  prompt with `input()` directly. {issue}`3572` {pr}`3653`
48	- Fix test failures when using pytest >= 9.1. {pr}`3656`
49	- {class}`Path` with `allow_dash=True` no longer triggers a `BytesWarning`,
50	  an error under `python -bb`, when checking a value against the `-`
51	  convention. {issue}`2877` {pr}`3642`
52	- Add {func}`custom_version_option`, a `--version` option whose output is
53	  produced by a callback, covering cases {func}`version_option` intentionally
54	  does not. The feature set of {func}`version_option` is now frozen; see
55	  [discussion #3527](https://github.com/pallets/click/discussions/3527). {pr}`3581`
56	- `style()` and `secho()` no longer silently drop the 256-color index `0`
57	  (black) passed as `fg` or `bg`, and now validate color arguments. Invalid
58	  colors raise a `ValueError` instead of a `TypeError`. {pr}`3677`
59	- The automatic help option stores its value under the reserved name
60	  `_click_default_help` instead of `help`, so a parameter named `help` no
61	  longer breaks parsing. The new name is visible in
62	  {meth}`Command.to_info_dict` output. Parameters that overwrite each other's
63	  value trigger a warning: an argument sharing its name with another
64	  parameter, or any parameter claiming the reserved name. Options may still
65	  share a name to compete for the same value (feature switches).
66	  {issue}`2819` {pr}`3678`
67	- `unstyle` and the ANSI handling behind help-text wrapping now strip the full
68	  CSI escape-sequence grammar. {pr}`3681`
69	- Streamline `Option` flag handling: the flag-kind, type, lazy-default and
70	  validation steps in `Option.__init__` move into focused helpers, and
71	  `flag_value` and `default` keep their unset sentinel at construction
72	  (resolved lazily on read) so `is UNSET` reliably tells a user-supplied value
73	  from an auto-derived one. Runtime behavior is unchanged, but
74	  {meth}`Parameter.to_info_dict` now resolves `default=True` on a feature
75	  switch to its `flag_value`, matching what the function receives at call
76	  time. {pr}`3641`

78	  will be removed in Click 9.0. {issue}`3481` {pr}`3695`
79	- The following `click.utils` names were never intentionally public and are
80	  now private (`_`-prefixed). The old names remain available with a
81	  `DeprecationWarning` until Click 9.0: `LazyFile`, `KeepOpenFile`,
82	  `make_default_short_help`, `PacifyFlushWrapper`, and `safecall`.
83	  {issue}`3099` {pr}`3695`

85	  {func}`os.chdir`, which mutates process-global state and is not
86	  thread-safe. The helper predates Python 3 and modern pytest: use a
87	  temporary directory ({class}`tempfile.TemporaryDirectory` or pytest's
88	  `tmp_path` fixture) with absolute paths instead. For running tests in

99	- {func}`get_pager_file` yields a text stream on Windows again. The temporary

127	
128	Released 2026-06-24
129	
130	- Fix Fish shell completion broken in `8.4.0` by {pr}`3126`. Newlines and
131	  tabs in option help text are now escaped, keeping the original completion
132	  format while still supporting multi-line help. {issue}`3502`

194	## Showing Environment Variables
195	
196	To control the appearance of environment variables pass `show_envvar`.
197	
198	```{eval-rst}
199	.. click:example::
200	
201	    @click.command()
202	    @click.option('--username', envvar='USERNAME', show_envvar=True)
203	    def greet(username):
204	        click.echo(f'Hello {username}!')
205	
206	.. click:run::
207	    invoke(greet, args=['--help'])
208	```

646	## Values from Environment Variables
647	
648	To pass in a value from a specific environment variable use `envvar`.
649	
650	```{eval-rst}
651	.. click:example::
652	
653	    @click.command()
654	    @click.option('--username', envvar='USERNAME')
655	    def greet(username):
656	       click.echo(f"Hello {username}!")
657	
658	.. click:run::
659	
660	    invoke(greet, env={'USERNAME': 'john'})
661	```
662	
663	If a list is passed to `envvar`, the first environment variable found is picked.
664	
665	```{eval-rst}
666	.. click:example::
667	
668	    @click.command()
669	    @click.option('--username', envvar=['ALT_USERNAME', 'USERNAME'])
670	    def greet(username):
671	       click.echo(f"Hello {username}!")
672	
673	.. click:run::
674	
675	    invoke(greet, env={'ALT_USERNAME': 'Bill', 'USERNAME': 'john'})
676	
677	```
678	
679	Variable names are:
680	 - [Case-insensitive on Windows but not on other platforms](https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/aa9eb5f757ceff461e6e996f12c89e5d9b583b01/Lib/os.py#L777-L789).
681	 - Not stripped of whitespace and should match the exact name provided to the
682	   `envvar` argument.
683	
684	For flag options, there are two concepts to consider: the activation of the flag
685	driven by the environment variable, and the value of the flag if it is
686	activated.
687	
688	The values read from environment variables are always strings and will require
689	extra processing. We need to transform these strings into boolean values that
690	will determine if the flag is activated or not.
